The primary outcome was median progression-free survival (mPFS). text: Sunitinib acts as a multi-targeted tyrosine kinase inhibitor that binds to the intracellular ATP-binding pocket of the KIT receptor, effectively blocking its autophosphorylation and downstream oncogenic signaling pathways [PMID: 42762362]. In Gastrointestinal Stromal Tumors (GIST), where activating mutations in *KIT* drive constitutive kinase activity and uncontrolled cell proliferation, sunitinib serves as a critical therapeutic backbone for patients who have progressed on first-line imatinib [PMID: 42762362, PMID: 42706100]. Mechanistically, sunitinib functions as a type II inhibitor, stabilizing the inactive conformation of the kinase, which complements the activity of newer type I inhibitors like bezuclastinib in combination strategies to overcome polyclonal secondary resistance [PMID: 42690334].
